text: I’ll stage a small offline adapter around the existing UDP runner, with focused checks for the 11ax protocol/data gate and recovery behavior. I’ll leave all hardware, Windows, network, and credential actions to the root agent.

The existing runner already has the required workload, single serial session, owned host cleanup, and original-only recovery. I’ll reuse that path and add a candidate staging shim plus an association-time gate; a failed mode or ping check will exit before any throughput worker starts.

The candidate pair is now staged and its payloads, config, sector padding, and original restore ranges verify offline. I also found the filesystem runner’s exact new proof schema (`korvo-fs-stdio-window-fixed-three-v1`); I’m adding that explicit layout while retaining the one-hour timestamp and complete readback/reset checks.

Root found that the working E95 control lost all host warmup pings while UDP succeeded. I’ll keep pings as observations and use the first original 30-second UDP RX run as the bounded data screen. TX will start only after positive board receive data and verified cleanup.

The revised adapter passes 11 offline tests, including E95’s failed warmup ping log followed by successful UDP, zero RX data skipping TX, wrong protocol/PHY stopping all load, and cleanup failure blocking recovery UART access. I’m finishing the pinned handoff and execute/recover instructions under the xts-board-evidence workflow.
